The temperature series — every progress curve

Exps 14–19 · 4OMe-BnOH · pH 7.00 · phosphate · 24 curves

All 24 curves of the temperature series, in temperature order. The rust line is whichever form the curve earned — one relaxation or two — from summary_kinetics.fit_progress, the dashed verticals are that fit's own clocks (τ, and τ₂ where its profile interval resolves), and the dotted line is its asymptote c − ΣB + v_ss·t. Every parameter of the function printed in each header is therefore visible on the drawing: v_ss as the asymptote's slope, ΣB as its distance from the curve at t = 0, τ as a rule.

Do not put v_ss on an Arrhenius plot where two phases were selected — it is an extrapolation far outside the data and comes out negative on two of the 35 °C curves. Section 4 uses v_peak, marked on each derivative strip at its maximum, which is where the fitted rate actually peaks rather than where a window says it does.

The grey break n (piecewise fit) verticals are the breakpoints of the best piecewise-linear description (curve_metrics.segment_selection), one or two according to an F test — a different estimator from the relaxation form drawn over them, which is why they are bracketed. Read the pattern in the footer, not the number of breaks: three straight lines fit a smooth bend better than two whether or not anything happened, so the count is a statement about approximation and the sequence of slopes is the statement about the curve. Nothing is excluded and every fit is computed on every point — except the instrument's first reading, which is discarded from every run in the archive (fit_dataset.DROP_FIRST_READING) and is therefore not plotted, fitted or scored here.

Read down a column and the induction shortens: the curves bend from lag-shaped at 15 °C to plainly decelerating at 40 °C, which is the same thing τ and the breakpoint ratio report as numbers.
